answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to stake a scarce token and earn access to higher-value jobs only through completed, dispute-free work. A knoll of fresh accounts then cannot cheaply pose as a trusted supplier: each must lock capital, while one fraudulent delivery can trigger a challenge that slashes its stake and the anchor identities that vouched for it. The jetty is narrow by design: attackers pay real capital and time for each identity, and risk losing both.
